correctness.rationale: The published Type-A single-deletion edge equivalence is directly checked in the original proof. A self-contained new argument rules out triple-distinct symbols at any coordinate, then uses exact twofold coverage by the three differing intervals to force one unique long edge and two adjacent short edges, each of length at least two. This is a bijection with the enumerated phase-splice parameters and proves the rational generating series for every integer q>=2,n>=1. The actual standalone verifier performs literal deletion-set comparisons on sixteen complete instances, enumerates every triangle on nineteen instances, and checks structure and all formula values. Finite checks are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known: xy is an edge iff it is an alternating two-symbol flip on one interval; a graph edge-count record follows. New: a triangle must have a unique longest flip interval, partitioned by the two other flip intervals into two adjacent segments of length at least two; this normal form yields q(q-1) times the convolution (n-ell+1)(ell-3)q^(n-ell) and its rational GF. Neither the pair count nor the binary clique-cover upper bound supplies an exact all-q triangle census. The ordinary one-read triangle result does not transfer by restriction without accounting for which edges survive.

originality.rationale: The published Type-A theorem and two-read graph clique-cover work supply the edge definition and contextual constructions, but the inspected primary sections do not enumerate unordered triangles or prove the unique long-edge and adjoining short-edge structure for all q and n. The nearest published record counts graph edges, and the other published triangle count concerns the strictly larger one-read confusability graph. Multiple targeted published-finding corpus searches did not identify the new enumeration; absence of hits is not assumed to prove uniqueness. An implicit equivalent result in unindexed coding literature is a genuine remaining risk.

value.rationale: The two-read deletion reconstruction conflict graph is a central finite-block coding object, and counting its triangles gives the first genuinely three-way incidence statistic beyond the known exact edge count. The proof supplies a complete all-alphabet/all-blocklength classification and exact rational generating function, not an arbitrary small enumeration. Three-clique abundance is a motivated invariant for multiple-read code obstructions and clique/independence analyses, although no stronger code-size theorem is claimed.
